# Configuration reference

<!-- Generated by `cargo xtask gen` from the settings declared in `crates/cortex-config/src/schema/sections.rs`. Do not edit: change the declaration and regenerate. -->

Every key a Cortex-Harness configuration file may hold. The design is in [architecture/08-configuration.md](../architecture/08-configuration.md): layers, merge rules, profiles, reloading and the trust rules. A JSON Schema of the same keys, for editors, is in [schema.json](schema.json).

**How to read the tables.**

- **Type.** A length of time is text such as `"20s"`, `"10m"` or `"1h30m"` (units `ms`, `s`, `m`, `h`, `d`). A list marked *joined* is added to by every layer; any other list, like any other value, is replaced by a higher layer.
- **From a project.** What happens to the key in a project's `.cortex/config.toml` or `.cortex/config.local.toml`. *preference*: applied always. *runs code* and *widens access*: applied only after the user has trusted the project, and listed for the user until then. *user only*: ignored, with a warning. A few keys depend on the value, and say how.
- **Takes effect.** When a change to the key reaches a running harness: *at once*, at the *next epoch* (it shapes the prompt, the tool list or the model), or after a *restart*.
- **Enforced.** In `[permissions]`, `[sandbox]` and `[limits]` an unknown key or value is an error and the file is refused: a restriction this version does not understand is never skipped. Everywhere else an unknown key is a warning.

## Top level

| Key | Type | Default | From a project | Takes effect | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `config_version` | whole number, 1 to 1000000 | `1` | preference | restart | The version of the configuration schema the file was written for. A file with a newer version than this build understands is refused. |
| `profile` | text | not set | user only | next epoch | The profile to apply: the name of a `[profiles.<name>]` table. The `--profile` flag overrides it. A project's file may define profiles and may not select one: a profile the user wrote is applied with the user's rights, so a repository that could pick it could switch on whatever the user's loosest profile allows. |

## `[managed]`

| Key | Type | Default | From a project | Takes effect | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `managed.locked` | list of text | `[]` | user only | at once | Keys that no layer above the managed file may change. A table's name locks every key in it. Read from the managed file only. |

## `[model]`

| Key | Type | Default | From a project | Takes effect | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `model.main` | text | not set | preference | next epoch | The model for the agent's own turns. Needed to run a turn. |
| `model.fast` | text | not set | preference | next epoch | The model for utility calls: summaries, titles. Without one, the main model is used. |
| `model.judge` | text | not set | preference | next epoch | The model for model-graded comparisons. Without one, the main model is used. |
| `model.effort` | text | not set | preference | next epoch | The reasoning level of the main role: one of the model's own levels, or `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high` or `max`. |
| `model.reasoning` | `"summary"`, `"none"` | `"summary"` | preference | next epoch | How much of the model's reasoning is shown. |
| `model.max_output` | whole number, 1 to 10000000 | not set | preference | next epoch | The most output tokens one response may have. Without it, the model's own limit applies. |
| `model.speed` | text | `"standard"` | by value: `standard` is a preference, any other tier raises cost | at once | The session's speed tier, which the main role runs at: `standard`, `fast` where the model offers it, or a provider's own tier name. The utility roles do not follow it: they run at `standard` unless `model.roles.<role>.speed` says otherwise. A project's file may set `standard`; any other tier costs more, and waits for the user to trust the project. |
| `model.speed_fallback` | `true` or `false` | `true` | preference | at once | Whether a request that a speed tier refuses is sent again at `standard`. When off, such a refusal is an ordinary rate limit. |
| `model.speed_wait` | length of time | `"20s"` | preference | at once | The longest one request waits in place for a speed tier before it falls back to `standard`. `"0s"` never waits. |
| `model.speed_cooldown` | length of time | `"10m"` | preference | at once | How long requests stay at `standard` after a fallback, when the provider does not say when the tier is available again. |
| `model.roles.*.provider` | text | not set | preference | next epoch | The provider that serves the role's model. Needed only when two providers have a model with the same name. |
| `model.roles.*.effort` | text | not set | preference | next epoch | The role's reasoning level. For `main` it overrides `model.effort`. |
| `model.roles.*.speed` | text | not set | by value: `standard` is a preference, any other tier raises cost | at once | The role's speed tier. For `main` it overrides `model.speed`. From a project's file, a tier other than `standard` waits for trust. |

## `[providers]`

| Key | Type | Default | From a project | Takes effect | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `providers.*.enabled` | `true` or `false` | `true` | user only | next epoch | Whether the provider is available. `false` removes an entry that a lower layer or the built-in table defines. |
| `providers.*.protocol` | text | not set | user only | next epoch | The wire protocol the endpoint speaks. |
| `providers.*.base_url` | text | not set | user only | next epoch | The endpoint's base URL. |
| `providers.*.key_env` | text | not set | user only | at once | The environment variable that holds the provider's API key. It is looked at before the credential store. |
| `providers.*.headers` | table of text, or `{ env = "NAME" }` | not set | user only | at once | Extra headers for every request. A value is text, or `{ env = "NAME" }` to read an environment variable when used. |
| `providers.*.idle_timeout` | length of time | not set | user only | at once | How long a response stream may be silent before the request fails. Overrides `retry.idle_timeout` for this provider. |
| `providers.*.first_event_timeout` | length of time | not set | user only | at once | How long to wait for the first event of a response. Overrides `retry.first_event_timeout` for this provider. |

## `[retry]`

| Key | Type | Default | From a project | Takes effect | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `retry.attempts` | whole number, 1 to 20 | `5` | preference | at once | The most attempts for one request, the first included. |
| `retry.backoff_base` | length of time | `"1s"` | preference | at once | The wait before the second attempt. Each later wait is this multiplied by `backoff_factor` again, up to `backoff_cap`. |
| `retry.backoff_factor` | number, 1 to 10 | `2.0` | preference | at once | What the wait is multiplied by after each attempt. |
| `retry.backoff_cap` | length of time | `"30s"` | preference | at once | The longest wait between two attempts. |
| `retry.max_wait` | length of time | `"2m"` | preference | at once | The longest wait a provider may ask for. A longer one ends the turn with the error and the provider's hint. |
| `retry.idle_timeout` | length of time | `"1m30s"` | preference | at once | How long a response stream may be silent before the request fails. |
| `retry.first_event_timeout` | length of time | `"1m"` | preference | at once | How long to wait for the first event of a response. |

## `[permissions]`

| Key | Type | Default | From a project | Takes effect | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `permissions.mode` | `"read-only"`, `"supervised"`, `"guided"`, `"autonomous"`, `"unrestricted"` | `"supervised"` | by level: not above the mode in effect is a preference, up to `supervised` widens access, above it user only | at once | The session's level: how much runs without asking. Enforced. |
| `permissions.rules` | list of rule: `effect`, `match`, `action`, joined | `[]` | by action: `deny` and `ask` are preferences, `allow` widens access | at once | Permission rules. Every layer adds to the list; `deny` beats `ask` beats `allow`, whatever the order. Enforced. |

## `[sandbox]`

| Key | Type | Default | From a project | Takes effect | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `sandbox.enabled` | `true` or `false` | `true` | user only | at once | Whether commands are confined by the OS sandbox where there is one. Enforced. |
| `sandbox.write` | list of text, joined | `[]` | widens access | at once | Paths a command may write besides the workspace. Every layer adds to the list. Enforced. |
| `sandbox.protect` | list of text, joined | `[]` | preference | at once | Paths a command may not change, besides the built-in ones. Every layer adds to the list. Enforced. |
| `sandbox.network` | `"off"`, `"full"` | `"off"` | by value: `off` is a preference, `full` widens access | at once | Whether a command may use the network. Enforced. |

## `[session]`

| Key | Type | Default | From a project | Takes effect | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `session.data_dir` | text | not set | user only | restart | The data directory. A leading `~` is the home directory. Without it the platform's usual place is used. |

## `[compat]`

| Key | Type | Default | From a project | Takes effect | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `compat.instructions` | `true` or `false` | `true` | user only | next epoch | Instruction files: `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md`. |
| `compat.mcp` | `true` or `false` | `true` | user only | next epoch | MCP server definitions of other clients, offered for import. |

## `[log]`

| Key | Type | Default | From a project | Takes effect | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `log.level` | text | not set | user only | at once | The level (`error`, `warn`, `info`, `debug` or `trace`), optionally followed by levels for target prefixes: `"info,cortex_llm=debug"`. The `CORTEX_LOG` variable and `--log-level` override it. |

## Reserved sections

These sections belong to parts of the harness that are not built yet. A file may already hold them: what is in them is kept and not checked. The build step that owns a section declares its keys, and they then move into the tables above. Until then a project's file cannot set anything in a section marked *user only*, and a section marked *runs code* waits for trust.

| Section | From a project | What it will hold |
|---|---|---|
| `[providers.*.capabilities]` | user only | Capability flags of the endpoint. |
| `[models]` | user only | Catalog overrides and additions by model name: limits, prices, reasoning control, capability flags. |
| `[http]` | user only | The HTTP client: the connect timeout, a proxy, and extra certificate authorities. |
| `[tools]` | user only | Enabled tools, output limits and per-tool settings. |
| `[shell]` | user only | The shell that runs commands: program, arguments, time limits. |
| `[context]` | user only | The compaction trigger and settings, and instruction file names. |
| `[verify]` | runs code | The verification mode, commands and time limits. |
| `[adapt]` | user only | Variant overrides per model, and the map and profile budgets. |
| `[stats]` | user only | Whether local statistics are recorded, and for how long. |
| `[index]` | user only | The repository map's caps. |
| `[runs]` | user only | The run engine: concurrency, workspaces, budgets. |
| `[usage]` | user only | The usage view: week start, ranges, the opt-in refresh and the other tools whose records may be read. |
| `[tui]` | user only | The terminal UI: presenter, theme, density. |
| `[keys]` | user only | Key bindings by mode. |
| `[terminal]` | user only | Terminal capability overrides. |
| `[rpc]` | user only | The RPC server: socket path, token, client timeouts. |
| `[hooks]` | runs code | Hooks by name. |
| `[extensions]` | runs code | Extensions by name. |
| `[skills]` | user only | Where skills are looked for. |
| `[mcp]` | runs code | MCP servers by name, and MCP settings. |
